newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Former MTRC chief rails against Legco fares plan.
newsitem.headline: Former MTRC chief rails against Legco fares plan.

text.p: The enactment of a bill to place railway fares under the control of Hong Kong's Legislative Council could hurt the credit ratings of the Mass Transit Railway Corp and Hong Kong, a former MTRC chief said Wednesday.

"It is my considered opinion that if LegCo took the explicit statutory power to veto fare changes determined by the corporation's board, financial confidence in the corporation would be seriously damaged," Wilfrid Newton, former chairman of the MTRC and the London Underground, told a Legco Transport Panel on Wednesday.
The result could be reduction of the MTRC's good credit rating, he said.
"A further consequence would be growing political concern that could affect Hong Kong's credit ratings and standing in international financial markets," he said.
The Amendment Bills were proposed by LegCo member Sin Chung Kai to give legislators the power to veto any fare adjustments determined by the railway corporation.
The MTRC is a top Hong Kong credit and is generally considered a benchmark for international debt issues of Hong Kong companies in the absense of a sovereign benchmark.
